content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes Grouped Self-Attention (GSA) and Compressed Cross-Attention (CCA) to solve memory and computational challenges in Transformer model. Results on three datasets show that it can outperform baselines while utilizes less compute and memory.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength

* The idea of grouped self-attention is intuitive and simple, following previous location attention + global attention pipeline.
* Results on three benchmark datasets show that it can outperform several baselines, e.g. Informer and Linformer while requiring less compute and memory per layer.

Weaknesses

* Although the idea is simple, it's hardly novel since previous works have explored this two level attention [1]. In addition, other state-of-the-art time series forecasting methods are not compared [2, 3]. 
* Experiments are only conducted on three datasets. I would like to suggest authors add more experiments and multiple evaluation metric to measure model performance.
*  Compressed Cross-Attention (CCA) is hardly novel and more like a project trick rather than a formal method.

[1] Poolingformer: Long Document Modeling with Pooling Attention
[2] Autoformer: Decomposition Transformers with Auto-Correlation for Long-Term Series Forecasting
[3] Pyraformer: Low-Complexity Pyramidal Attention for Long-Range Time Series Modeling and Forecasting
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is easy to follow while its quality is not high given its limited novelty compared to recently proposed methods. See more in Weakness section. Reproducing its results may take some time as no source code and exact hyper-parameters are provided.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposes Grouped Self-Attention (GSA) and Compressed Cross-Attention (CCA) to solve memory and computational challenges in Transformer model. However,  GSA is hardly novel compared to Poolingformer and comparisons with recent state-of-the-art Transformer time series forecasting models are not conducted. In addition, experiments are mainly conducted on three datasets and I would like to suggest authors to add datasets and evaluation in their experiments.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 2: You are willing to defend your assessment, but it is quite likely that you did not understand the central parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
This article propose a new transformer module relying on compression to reduce the complexity. The first proposal consists in a hierarchical attention: a first attention is computed locally and then, group representers (compressed representations) are compared at the global scale. This architecture reduce the complexity of the transformer architecture.
After a state of the art and a model section, the authors carry out experiments on classical multivariate datasets: the number of experiments is rather limited but corresponds to what is done in the literature.
The authors propose an interesting ablation study that illustrate the interest of the global compressed represntation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Section 2.1 is probably useless in ICLR

GSA seems directly inspired by hierarchical decomposition. However, in spite of a consequent state of the art, it is very difficult to understand precisely the contribution of the authors compared to the classical references of the field in terms of efficiency
I wonder if GSA can be viewed as a specific case (local+global), illustrated in Longformer, Figure 2(d)
Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer.
How do the authors position themself with respect to other hierarchical transformers? Is the compression mechanism a specific way to agregate hierarchical informations?

use \ell instead of l in math mode

d should be defined clearly. Is it the number of channel in a multivariate TS or is it the hidden layer dimension of a CNN inherited from the Informer architecture?
This is a critical part of the proposed architecture: a sentence like: "Our proposed model is based on the Informer framework" is definitely not sufficient to undestand this point.
For univariate time series, is d equals to 1?

In the complexity computation, I think it is not possible to remove m, which is proportional to l. As a consequence, I don't think that the complexity is really O(l), more likely O(m^2+ml).

L_g and l_s are probably very sensitive (both on the performance and on the memory requirement.)

Fig 3 (left) is not readable: should be passed to log-scale

In section 4.2.1, the authors insist on the fact that all considered references are very close to each other. The authors could have considered frankly different references such as RNN or SARIMA/Prophet in order to properly differentiate the contributions of different stages.

I don't understand the last sentence of 4.2.1: Because all the methods shared the Informer framework including global time stamp embedding and generative style decoder, the only difference was the mechanism of self-attention, and thus the baselines other than Informer performed better as well.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Except for the model entry (inherited from another article), everything is pretty clear in the article and reproducibility seems assured. The contribution is limited but present.
content.summary_of_the_review: This proposal describe an interesting architecture, but I am not completely convinced by the positioning of the contributions in relation to the state of the art. In the same way, if the experiments show a gain compared to the reference models, I do not understand from which assumptions this gain comes. Finally, I think that the model complexity calculation is a bit optimistic. For all these reasons, my judgment on the article is not positive.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: To alleviate the efficiency issue in time series, this paper proposes two novel modules, Grouped Self-Attention (GSA) and Compressed Cross-Attention (CCA). With GSA and CCA, they can achieve a computational space and time complexity of order with a sequence length  under small hyperparameter limitations. The extensive experiments show the effectiveness of their proposed modules.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: Complexity is one main issue in time series since long dependency is considerable. This paper proposes two modules to solve this problem. 

Weaknesses: 
(i) This paper proposes two modules for complexity reduction. However, techniques used have been proposed before. For example, grouped self-attention has been proposed in Reformer, and linear projection has been proposed in Linformer. Thus, this paper is a kind of ensemble in my view, which lacks novelty.
(ii) In Table 1, the improvement is not significant. Even in some settings, the proposed method is not better than the previous baselines.
(iii) Can you provide some analysis for the case where the proposed methods fail in Table 1?

content.summary_of_the_review: Long dependency is a considerable case for time series and this paper proposes two modules - GSA and CCA for complexity reduction. However, since both techniques have been applied in previous papers in NLP field. I think the novelty is somehow weak in this paper. Furthermore, the experiment results are not significant in the paper.
